theory.intro: Goods bought on terms usually cost more than paying upfront because interest is added. Interest-free instalments paid without fees can equal the upfront price. **Buying on terms** means a deposit and then regular instalments; **buy now, pay later** splits the price into interest-free instalments. Work out the total paid, then compare it with the cash price.
facts: $\text{Extra paid}=\text{Total paid on terms}-\text{Cash price}$, which is also the saving made by paying cash.
A deposit quoted as a percentage is that percentage of the **cash price**, and the balance owing is the cash price minus the deposit.

Buy now, pay later schemes have different terms and conditions. For an interest-free purchase without fees, the instalments add to the purchase price; calculate late fees using the conditions supplied.
steps: Find the deposit, taking the percentage of the cash price if it is quoted as a percentage.
Multiply the number of instalments by the instalment amount.
Add the deposit to the instalments to get the total paid.
Subtract the cash price from the total paid to find the extra paid.

workedExamples.question_text:
A camping set costs $\$1\,080$ cash, or a $\$120$ deposit and $24$ monthly instalments of $\$50$.
(a) Calculate the total paid on terms.
(b) Find the interest charged and the saving made by paying cash.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Total paid:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Total paid}&=\text{Deposit}+\text{Number of instalments}\times\text{Instalment amount}\\&=120+24\times50\\&=\$1\,320\end{aligned}$
(b) Interest charged:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Interest}&=\text{Total paid}-\text{Cash price}\\&=1\,320-1\,080\\&=\$240\end{aligned}$
Paying cash saves $\$240$.

workedExamples.question_text:
A sound system costs $\$1\,200$ cash, or a $15\%$ deposit and $26$ fortnightly instalments of $\$45$.
Calculate the deposit, the total paid on terms and the saving made by paying cash.

A furniture package costs a total of $\$2\,760$ on terms, including a $\$360$ deposit. The remainder, including interest, is paid in $24$ equal monthly repayments.
Calculate each monthly repayment.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Amount to repay after the deposit:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}2\,760-360\\&=\$2\,400\end{aligned}$
Monthly repayment:
$\begin{aligned}\text{Repayment}&=\text{Total owing}\div\text{Number of repayments}\\&=2\,400\div24\\&=\$100\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text:
A computer costs $\$1\,500$. It is bought on terms with a $20\%$ deposit and simple interest charged at $8\%$ p.a. on the remaining balance for $18$ months.
Calculate the total cost of buying the computer on terms.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Deposit:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}0.20\times1\,500\\&=\$300\end{aligned}$
Balance owing:
$\begin{aligned}P&=1\,500-300\\&=\$1\,200\end{aligned}$
Convert the term to years: $n=18\div12=1.5$.
Interest on the balance:
$\begin{aligned}I&=Prn\\&=1\,200\times0.08\times1.5\\&=\$144\end{aligned}$
Total cost, including the deposit:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}300+1\,200+144\\&=\$1\,644\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text:
A second-hand car costs $\$10\,500$. A buyer pays a $\$2\,500$ deposit and repays the balance over $3$ years in equal monthly repayments. Simple interest is charged at $9\%$ p.a. on the balance after the deposit.
Calculate each monthly repayment, to the nearest cent.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Balance owing:
$\begin{aligned}P&=10\,500-2\,500\\&=\$8\,000\end{aligned}$
Interest on the balance:
$\begin{aligned}I&=Prn\\&=8\,000\times0.09\times3\\&=\$2\,160\end{aligned}$
Total owing after the deposit:
$\begin{aligned}A&=P+I\\&=8\,000+2\,160\\&=\$10\,160\end{aligned}$
There are $3\times12=36$ monthly repayments.
Monthly repayment:
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}10\,160\div36\\&\approx\$282.22\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text:
Shoes costing $\$320$ are bought through an interest-free scheme with $4$ equal instalments and no other purchase fees. Maximum total late fees are the lower of $25\%$ of the order value or $\$68$.
(a) Calculate each instalment.
(b) Find the interest paid if all instalments are paid on time.
(c) Calculate the maximum total late fees.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) Each instalment is $320\div4=\$80$.
(b) The total paid is $4\times80=\$320$, so the interest paid is $\$0$.
(c) $25\%\times320=\$80$.
The lower of $\$80$ and $\$68$ is $\$68$, so the maximum total late fees are $\$68$.

workedExamples.question_text:
An order costing $\$56$ is bought through an interest-free instalment scheme. A missed payment incurs an initial late fee of $\$10$ and a further fee of up to $\$7$ if it remains unpaid $7$ days later. Total late fees are capped at the lower of $25\%$ of the order value or $\$68$.
The initial fee has already been charged. Calculate the further late fee after $7$ days.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Maximum total late fees:
$25\%\times56=\$14$.
The lower of $\$14$ and $\$68$ is $\$14$.
Amount remaining under the cap:
$14-10=\$4$.
The further fee is reduced to $\$4$ to keep total late fees within the cap.

foundation.question_text:
A refrigerator has a cash price of $\$1\,450$.
It can be bought on terms for a $\$150$ deposit and $12$ monthly instalments of $\$124.50$.
Calculate the total amount paid for the refrigerator on terms.

A bicycle has a cash price of $\$960$.
On terms it costs a $\$120$ deposit and $26$ fortnightly instalments of $\$38.50$.
Calculate the total amount paid for the bicycle on terms.

A washing machine costs $\$1\,190$ cash, or a $\$200$ deposit and $18$ monthly instalments of $\$62.75$.
How much more than the cash price is paid by buying on terms?

An electric scooter costs $\$1\,320$ cash, or a $\$180$ deposit and $52$ weekly instalments of $\$25.60$.
How much more than the cash price is paid by buying on terms?

A laptop has a cash price of $\$1\,800$.
On terms it can be bought for a $15\%$ deposit and $24$ monthly instalments of $\$78.25$.
Calculate the total amount paid for the laptop on terms.

After the deposit on a bedroom suite is paid, the balance owing including interest is $\$3\,150$.
It is repaid in $36$ equal monthly repayments.
Calculate each monthly repayment.

A phone costing $\$840$ is paid for using an interest-free buy now, pay later scheme in $4$ equal instalments.

An order costing $\$240$ is bought using an interest-free buy now, pay later scheme.
The maximum total late fees are the lower of $25\%$ of the order value or $\$68$.
Calculate the maximum amount payable in late fees.
foundation.solution_text:
$25\%\times\$240=\$60$
Since $\$60$ is less than $\$68$, the maximum amount payable in late fees is $\$60.00$.

A chest freezer costs $\$2\,700$.
It is bought on terms with a $\$700$ deposit, and the balance is repaid over $2$ years in $24$ equal monthly repayments with simple interest charged at $12\%$ p.a. on the balance owing.
Calculate each monthly repayment, to the nearest cent.
development.solution_text:
Balance owing:
$\$2\,700-\$700$
$=\$2\,000$
Interest on the balance:
$I=Prn$
$=\$2\,000\times0.12\times2$
$=\$480$
Total owing:
$\$2\,000+\$480$
$=\$2\,480$
Monthly repayment:
$\$2\,480\div24$
$\approx\$103.33$

It is bought on terms with a $\$350$ deposit, and the balance is repaid over $2$ years in $24$ equal monthly repayments with simple interest charged at $9\%$ p.a. on the balance owing.

development.solution_text:
Balance owing:
$\$1\,750-\$350=\$1\,400$
Interest on the balance:
$I=Prn$
$=\$1\,400\times0.09\times2$
$=\$252$
Total owing:
$\$1\,400+\$252=\$1\,652$
Monthly repayment:
$\$1\,652\div24\approx\$68.83$

An order costing $\$52$ is bought using an interest-free buy now, pay later scheme.
An initial late fee of $\$10$ is charged for a missed payment, with a further fee of up to $\$7$ if it remains unpaid $7$ days later.
Total late fees are capped at the lower of $25\%$ of the order value or $\$68$.
The initial fee has already been charged. Calculate the further late fee charged after $7$ days.
development.solution_text:
Late fee cap:
$25\%\times\$52=\$13$
Since $\$13$ is less than $\$68$, the cap is $\$13$.
Amount remaining under the cap:
$\$13-\$10=\$3$
The further late fee is reduced from $\$7$ to $\$3.00$.

mastery.question_text:
A television costs $\$3\,875$ cash.
It is bought on terms with a $\$625$ deposit, and the balance is repaid over $3$ years in $36$ equal monthly repayments with simple interest charged at $11.5\%$ p.a. on the balance owing.

A camera costs $\$1\,875$ cash.
It is bought on terms with a $\$375$ deposit, and the balance is repaid over $2$ years in $24$ equal monthly repayments with simple interest charged at $7.5\%$ p.a. on the balance owing.
Calculate each monthly repayment, to the nearest cent.
mastery.solution_text:
Balance owing:
$\$1\,875-\$375=\$1\,500$
Interest on the balance:
$I=Prn$
$=\$1\,500\times0.075\times2$
$=\$225$
Total owing:
$\$1\,500+\$225=\$1\,725$
Monthly repayment:
$\$1\,725\div24\approx\$71.88$
